text:
alex: Hey team — saw a sharp latency spike on dedicated-pool-3 around 14:02 UTC. p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s for short chats. Any visibility?

ravi: Noted. Saw throughput drop too. Autoscaler didn't kick; dedicated pool stayed at 4 GPUs.

jess: I'm seeing a pattern: bursts of tiny requests (<=8 tokens) from tenant X interleaving big batched requests. Batching heuristic seems to collapse into many small batches.

alex: Can you paste profiler dump? wondering if kernel selection changed or KV cache thrashing.

ravi: Dumping sample profiler from the window (14:01:30-14:03:00):

```
profile_summary {
  kernel_select_events: 87
  fallback_kernel: 42
  preferred_kernel_time_ms: 210
  fallback_kernel_time_ms: 520
  kv_cache_evictions: 310
  avg_batch_size: 3.2
}
```

ravi: fallback_kernel spikes align with latency spikes. Looks like for many sequences runtime chose a generic kernel path.

jess: That fallback count is huge. Could be due to mixed sequence lengths causing the kernel matcher to not find an optimized kernel.

olivia: Also noticed KV cache miss rate jumped from 2%->23% at the same time. If KV cache is evicting, many requests redo autoregressive work.

alex: Any dashboard traces for affected requests? I can't find trace IDs in the trace UI for those samples.

olivia: This is the observability gap — our trace sampling is rate-limited and we dropped traces for short requests. The request_id is present in logs but not linked to traces.

jess: Logs show a lot of runtime INFO lines, but our log-sampler is set to 1% for runtime to cut cost. We missed high-res logs when the incident hit.

sre-oncall: Alert for p99 latency fired at 14:05. I pulled the node metrics — GPU occupancy was low (~12%) on the affected GPUs while CPU spiked. Classic noisy-neighbor: many tiny async requests saturating scheduler.

alex: So hypothesis: tenant X sends many tiny requests -> batching heuristic creates many tiny batches -> kernel matcher falls back to generic kernels for certain seq lengths -> KV cache churn -> compute overhead and latency spikes. Observability gaps: traces sampled away, dashboards show aggregate GPU utilization which looked fine, but per-request latencies spiked.

ravi: Agree. Quick mitigations: 1) throttle tenant X (rate-limit small requests) 2) increase log sampling to 100% for runtime for 10m 3) force kernel matcher to prefer specialized kernel with tolerant length buckets (hotfix).

jess: I can push a config tweak to batching heuristics: set min_batch_timeout to 8ms and add a small-request queue to coalesce tiny ones. That will reduce tiny-batch churn.

olivia: I'll flip tracing sampling for runtime to 100% for the incident window and replay the missing traces. Also adding a dashboard tile that shows "fallback_kernel_rate" and "kv_cache_eviction_rate" side-by-side. Right now the dashboard has them on separate pages which hides correlation.

infra-bot: @alex deploy job started: runtime/heuristic-tweak v2 -> canary on dedicated-pool-3 (job id: deploy-99321).

alex: Thanks. After canary, we should watch fallback_kernel_count and avg_batch_size. If fallback falls and p99 recovers, keep and roll.

sre-oncall: I applied a temporary tenant throttle for X at 14:17 UTC. Observed p99 drop to ~160ms within 2 minutes. GPU occupancy rose to 68% (better batching).

ravi: Post-mortem action items:
- Short-term: batching heuristic tweak + tenant throttling (done)
- Mid-term: make kernel selection tolerant to small length variance; reduce strictness that causes fallback
- Observability: increase default trace sampling for runtime to 5% and keep adaptive on-alert ramp to 100%
- Dashboards: add combined panel for kernel_fallback vs kv_eviction with correlation smoothing
- Logging: raise runtime log-sample to 5% for 24h after any p99 incident

jess: I'll open a PR for heuristic and add unit tests that simulate mixed-length traffic.

olivia: I'll own dashboard + tracing changes and add runbook notes: when p99 spikes, flip traces/logs to 100% for 15m and enable tenant throttles.

alex: Great. Please tag all related PRs and follow up in this thread with links. Thanks for quick response :thumbsup:

jess: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/784 (heuristic change)

olivia: Dashboard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412

ravi: Follow-up: will run a load test simulating noisy neighbor patterns to validate changes.

alex: Closing the incident thread; keeping this pinned for postmortem notes.
